steps.title: Sustainability
steps.body: means meeting the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs. In chemistry, this means using resources responsibly and minimising environmental impact.

steps.title: Key idea 2
steps.body: The reduce, reuse, recycle principles help conserve finite resources and reduce waste and environmental impact.

steps.title: Corrosion
steps.body: is the deterioration of metals by reaction with substances in the environment. Rusting is the corrosion of iron, which requires both oxygen and water . Corrosion weakens metals and can be dangerous and expensive.

steps.title: Sacrificial protection
steps.body: works because a more reactive metal (e.g. zinc, magnesium) will oxidise in preference to iron. The more reactive metal sacrifices itself to protect the iron.

steps.title: Worked example
steps.body: Corrosion is the deterioration of metals by reaction with substances in the environment. Rusting is the corrosion of iron, which requires both oxygen and water . Corrosion weakens metals and can be dangerous and expensive. Iron + Oxygen + Water → Hydrated iron(III) oxide (rust) Both oxygen and water must be present for iron to rust. If either is absent, rusting does not occur. Prevention Method How It Works Example Painting Creates a barrier between the metal and air/water Car bodies, bridges, garden gates Oiling / greasing Creates a water-repellent barrier Bicycle chains, machine parts Galvanising Coating iron/steel with a layer of zinc .
